subject.title: ACP bridge should support Workbench session MCP for visible Mac-control tools

question: Should `openclaw acp` accept Workbench-supplied per-session stdio MCP servers, or should Workbench Mac-control use the existing OpenClaw-managed MCP/plugin configuration path?
rationale: Current source, tests, docs, and ACPX history intentionally keep the OpenClaw ACP bridge from consuming per-session MCP servers, and reversing that changes the command/secret/tool trust boundary.

options.title: Use Gateway-managed MCP or bundle plugin
options.body: Keep the ACP bridge MCP-free and document/package `evaos-mac-control` through OpenClaw `mcp.servers` or a bundle-style plugin with explicit tool policy and redacted proof.

options.title: Design default-off per-session MCP
options.body: Add ACP bridge session MCP only behind a maintainer-approved security design covering allowed transports, command/env validation, lifecycle cleanup, and tests.

options.title: Defer until Workbench runtime pin is fixed
options.body: Require Workbench to rerun proof on the intended current OpenClaw runtime before changing the bridge boundary.

recommendation.title: Use Gateway-managed MCP or bundle plugin
recommendation.body: Keep the ACP bridge MCP-free and document/package `evaos-mac-control` through OpenClaw `mcp.servers` or a bundle-style plugin with explicit tool policy and redacted proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete reviewed and landed the adjacent ACPX bridge-safe routing decision that explicitly kept OpenClaw bridge sessions from receiving configured MCP servers.
